subject: math
title: 4 questions from earlier lessons
instructions: Work every problem on paper first and show each step. Then type your answer and press Check. You get two tries on each question. Type a fraction like 3/4, a mixed number like 2 1/2, and a power like 3^4.

sections.name: Catch-up
sections.desc: Questions you missed before, with new numbers or a new story. Right on the first try takes one off your list.

items.q: A school wants to cover a play area with rubber safety mats. The mats cost $7 for each square foot, and the budget is $1,600. Design 1 is a square that is 15 feet on each side. Design 2 is a rectangle that is 11 feet by 21 feet.

ans.model: Design 1 costs $1,575, which is $25 under the $1,600 budget. Design 2 costs $1,617, which is $17 over the budget, so only Design 1 fits.
ans.look: Names both costs and compares each one with $1,600.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: Give the reason for your choice. Use both costs and the budget.

a: a) 15² = 225, so the square is 225 square feet.
b) 225 × 7 = 1,575, so Design 1 costs $1,575.
c) 11 × 21 = 231, so the rectangle is 231 square feet.
1,600 − 1,575 = 25, so Design 1 is $25 under the budget.
1,617 − 1,600 = 17, so Design 2 is $17 over the budget.
d) and e) Decision: Design 1, because $1,575 is within the $1,600 budget and $1,617 is not.
items.hint: Find the area of each design in square feet, then each cost. Put each cost next to the budget and ask: over or under?

items.q: The ones digits of the powers of 8 follow a pattern. Here are the first four powers: 8¹ is 8, 8² is 64, 8³ is 512 and 8⁴ is 4,096.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: What is the ones digit of 8⁶?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: 8¹ ends in 8. What is the next exponent that makes a power of 8 end in 8 again?

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: What is the ones digit of 8²⁴?

a: 32,768 × 8 = 262,144, so the ones digit of 8⁶ is 4.
b) The ones digits go 8, 4, 2, 6, and then 8 again at 8⁵. The cycle has 4 digits, so the next exponent is 5.
c) 24 ÷ 4 = 6, so 8²⁴ comes at the end of the sixth full cycle. Every full cycle ends in the digit 6.
Answers: a) 4, b) 5, c) 6
items.hint: Write only the ones digit of each power in a row: multiply the last ones digit by 8 and keep only its ones digit. Stop when 8 comes back.

items.q: Add the odd numbers in order, starting from 1, and look at the sums: 1 + 3 + 5 = 9, 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 16 and 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 = 25.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write your answer to part a as a power with exponent 2. Type it with the ^ key.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Use the pattern to find the sum of the first 12 odd numbers, 1 + 3 + 5 and so on up to 23.

a: b) 49 = 7 × 7 = 7², so adding the first 7 odd numbers gives 7².
c) Count the odd numbers from 1 to 23: (23 + 1) ÷ 2 = 12, so there are 12 of them.
12² = 144, so adding the first 12 odd numbers gives 144.
Answers: a) 49, b) 7², c) 144
items.hint: Compare each sum with how many odd numbers were added to make it. Before part c, check on paper that the list from 1 to 23 really holds 12 odd numbers.

items.q: In a video game, your coins double at the end of every level. You start with 1 coin. After level 1 you have 2 coins, after level 2 you have 4 coins, and after level 3 you have 8 coins.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many coins do you have after level 7?

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: After which level do you have more than 2,000 coins for the first time? Type the level number.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: After level 16 you have 2¹⁶ coins. Sixteen 2s multiplied together is the same as eight 2s times eight 2s, which is 2⁸ × 2⁸. Find the value of 2¹⁶.

a: a) 2⁷ = 128, so you have 128 coins after level 7.
b) 2¹⁰ = 1,024, which is less than 2,000.
2¹¹ = 2,048, which is more than 2,000, so the first time is after level 11.
Answers: a) 128, b) level 11, c) 65,536
items.hint: For part c, find 2⁸ first, then multiply it by itself in two pieces. Check each digit of your product before you type it.
